notes: §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SR3: "Identical user-defined names may appear in a source program; however, uniqueness must then be established through qualification for each user-defined name explicitly referenced, except in the case of redefinition. All available qualifiers need not be specified so long as uniqueness is established." The procedure division half conforms: QualifiedCandidates returns every declaration whose ancestors carry the written qualifiers in order, gaps allowed and a file-name outermost (QualifierWalk), ResolveUnqualified, ResolveQualified and UniqueOrReportAmbiguous refuse any count but one with COBOL1639, ResolveProcedureWord does the same for a paragraph-name (COBOL2121) and looks only in the referencing program, and ReportOf refuses an unqualified PAGE-COUNTER or LINE-COUNTER under two reports (COBOL2729). None of these has an edition arm. Probed at --std 85: partial, gapped and full qualifier chains with OF and IN, a file-name qualifier, a qualified condition-name, an unqualified REDEFINES of a non-unique name and P OF S all resolve; an unqualified or under-qualified non-unique data-name or condition-name, qualifiers in the wrong order, an ambiguous paragraph-name, a contained program's PERFORM or GO TO of the containing program's procedure-name and a non-unique FILE STATUS data-name are refused. The data division half does not: the clauses of a data description entry take the 2002 exemption at 85. EntryClauseCandidates (OCCURS DEPENDING ON, called by OdoResolvePass.Run) and SubtreeCandidates (OCCURS KEY IS in OccursKeyResolvePass.Run, RENAMES in ResolveRedefinesPass.Run) narrow the candidates to the subject's own group or record before they are counted, which is §2023:8.4.2.2.1 rule 5 ("the names of any group items superordinate to both the data-name and the subject of the data description entry clause are used as implicit qualifiers for the reference"), and no caller asks the edition. 1985 has that exemption for redefinition only (§1985:VI.5.10.3 SR7) and gives the other clauses the means to qualify (§1985:VI.5.8.3 SR2: "Data-name-1 and data-name-2 may be qualified."; §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR5); ISO/IEC 1989:2002 lists the exemption as its change (§2002:F.2 item 67: "Data-names referenced in a data description entry need not be qualified when they are defined in the same group as the subject of the entry"). Probed at --std 85, each accepted with no diagnostic: DEPENDING ON CNT with CNT in the table's record and in another record; ASCENDING KEY IS K with a second K in another record; 66 XY RENAMES X THRU Y with X and Y in another record too. A fourth case is accepted at every edition by a selection of the compiler's own: RECORD KEY IS K with a second K in working-storage (the local function InRecords of ResolveFiles prefers the candidate inside the file's records). The witness references FLD OF REC-A and FLD IN GRP-Y and displays AAA and BBB. No kb/Work note owns the fix.

next.reason: 1985 requires qualification of every non-unique referenced name 'except in the case of redefinition'. §2023:8.4.2.2.3 SR1 keeps 'uniqueness shall be established through a sequence of qualifiers'. But §2023:8.4.2.2.1 adds exemptions, among them 'The name is a data-name referenced in a data description entry clause whose subject is subordinate to the same group item as that data-name', with implicit qualifiers. So an unqualified non-unique OCCURS DEPENDING ON object that 1985 refused is accepted in 2023 (looser), and the VARYING and type-declaration exemptions cover new features. Special-register qualification is carried by 8.4.2.2.3 SR8 to SR10. The cross-program paragraph/section bar is the uncataloged §2023:8.4.6.1 ('may be referenced only by statements in the source element in which the user-defined word is declared').
